title: Tessellation Detail Control with Wireframe & Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a tessellation detail control system with wireframe preview and a physics debug overlay.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x0a0a0a). Renderer with antialiasing, sized to full window, responsive on resize.
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8), looking at origin.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- One AmbientLight (0x404040, intensity 0.5) and one DirectionalLight (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at position (5, 10, 5).
- Create a primary mesh: an IcosahedronGeometry with initial radius 2.0 and initial tessellation detail level 2. Use MeshStandardMaterial with color 0x3388ff and flatShading enabled.
- Create a wireframe overlay mesh: clone the same geometry, apply MeshBasicMaterial with color 0x00ff88, wireframe true. This overlay sits on top of the solid mesh (same position). Initially visible.
- Create a ground plane (PlaneGeometry 20x20) at y=-2.5, rotated to be horizontal, with MeshStandardMaterial color 0x222222.

## Tessellation Detail Control
- The tessellation detail level ranges from 0 to 6 (integer). Initial value is 2.
- Pressing UP arrow increases detail by 1 (clamped to max 6). Pressing DOWN arrow decreases detail by 1 (clamped to min 0).
- When detail changes, recreate the IcosahedronGeometry with the new detail, update both the solid mesh and wireframe overlay mesh geometries. Dispose old geometries properly.
- Track the vertex count and triangle count of the current geometry.

## Wireframe Toggle
- Pressing 'W' key toggles the wireframe overlay mesh visibility on/off.

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Simulate a simple bounding sphere for the icosahedron. The bounding sphere has center (0,0,0) and radius equal to the icosahedron radius (2.0).
- Simulate gravity: the icosahedron has a simulated y-velocity and y-position. Initially y-position is 0 (mesh at origin), y-velocity is 0, gravity is -9.81.
- Pressing 'G' key toggles physics simulation on/off. When on, each frame updates velocity += gravity * dt, position.y += velocity * dt. The floor is at y = -2.5 + radius (so the sphere rests on the ground plane). When the sphere hits the floor, clamp position and set velocity to -velocity * 0.5 (bounce with restitution 0.5). If abs(velocity) < 0.1 and position is at floor level, set velocity to 0 (rest state).
- Pressing 'R' key resets physics: position.y = 0, velocity = 0, and moves mesh back to y=0.
- When physics is active, render a debug wireframe sphere (WireframeGeometry of SphereGeometry matching bounding sphere radius) with LineSegments, color 0xff4444, that follows the mesh position. This debug sphere is only visible when physics is active.

## Render Mode Cycling
- Pressing 'M' key cycles the solid mesh material through 3 modes: 'standard' (MeshStandardMaterial, color 0x3388ff, flatShading), 'normal' (MeshNormalMaterial, flatShading), 'depth' (MeshDepthMaterial). Track current mode index (0, 1, 2).

## HUD / DOM UI
- Create a fixed-position HUD panel at top-left (CSS styled, semi-transparent dark background, white text, padding 15px, font-family monospace, z-index 100).
- Display: Tessellation Detail: {level}, Vertices: {count}, Triangles: {count}, Wireframe: ON/OFF, Physics: ON/OFF, Render Mode: standard/normal/depth, FPS: {value}, Physics Y-Pos: {value toFixed(2)}, Physics Y-Vel: {value toFixed(2)}.
- Update HUD every frame.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields, updated every frame:
  - tessellationDetail (integer 0-6)
  - vertexCount (integer, from geometry.attributes.position.count)
  - triangleCount (integer, vertexCount / 3 for non-indexed or index.count / 3 for indexed)
  - wireframeVisible (boolean)
  - physicsActive (boolean)
  - physicsYPos (number, current y position of mesh)
  - physicsYVel (number, current y velocity)
  - renderModeIndex (integer 0-2)
  - renderModeName (string: 'standard', 'normal', or 'depth')
  - debugSphereVisible (boolean)
  - boundingSphereRadius (number, should be 2.0)
  - meshPositionY (number, actual mesh.position.y)
  - fps (number)
  - frameCount (integer, incremented each frame)
  - groundLevel (number, the computed floor y for the sphere center: -2.5 + radius)
  - isResting (boolean, true when physics active and velocity is 0 and at floor)

## Animation Loop
- Use requestAnimationFrame. Compute delta time via THREE.Clock. Update physics if active. Update HUD. Render scene. Increment frameCount.
physics_constraints: Gravity is -9.81 m/s^2. Bounce restitution coefficient is 0.5. Floor collision at y = -2.5 + icosahedronRadius. Velocity damped to 0 when abs(velocity) < 0.1 and at floor level. Position must never go below groundLevel. Vertex count must match IcosahedronGeometry formula for given detail level.
